title: The Democrats Who Might Block Biden’s Infrastructure Plan

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日简报《Dealbook》的商业与政策报道。

sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的埃斯特·赫恩顿，代班迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, Congress faces a key vote on one of the president's top priorities, his $1 trillion infrastructure bill.
sentences.zh: 今天，国会将面临一项关键投票，对象是总统的首要任务之一，即他那价值1万亿美元的基础设施法案。

sentences.en: But now, members of his own party are threatening to block it.
sentences.zh: 但现在，他自己党内的成员正威胁要阻止它。

sentences.en: I spoke with my colleague, Emily Cochran, about the infighting in Congress, and with one progressive congresswoman about why she's willing to vote no.
sentences.zh: 我与我的同事艾米丽·科克伦讨论了国会内部的争斗，并与一位进步派女议员谈论了她为什么愿意投反对票。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, September 30th.
sentences.zh: 今天是9月30日，星期四。

sentences.en: Hey, Emily, how are you?
sentences.zh: 嘿，艾米丽，你好吗？

sentences.en: It's another day in paradise.
sentences.zh: 又是人间仙境的一天。

sentences.en: On the scale of 1 to 10, how bad is today?
sentences.zh: 如果按1到10分来分，今天有多糟糕？

sentences.en: You know, the limit does not exiSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，极限是不存在的。

sentences.en: I'm sure it's like, wherever you are right now, you already know tomorrow will be worse.
sentences.zh: 我敢说，无论你现在在哪里，你心里都已经知道明天会更糟。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm afraid if I give something specific, the Congress gods will just challenge me.
sentences.zh: 是的，我担心如果我说得太具体，国会的大神们就会直接来挑战我。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, we do appreciate you helping us out on a crazy week.
sentences.zh: 好吧，在这个疯狂的一周里，我们真的很感激你来帮忙。

sentences.en: And I feel like everything I've read from The Hill over the last couple weeks has required a professional translator.
sentences.zh: 我觉得过去几周我从国会山读到的所有内容都需要一个专业翻译。

sentences.en: So thank you for letting us use you as a professional translator.
sentences.zh: 所以谢谢你让我们把你当成专业翻译来用。

sentences.en: Well, I hope I can deliver because, unfortunately, there's a lot of garble right now.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我希望我能不负众望，因为不幸的是，现在有太多乱七八糟的信息了。

sentences.en: I know that there's a lot of moving parts happening at once.
sentences.zh: 我知道现在有很多变数同时在发生。

sentences.en: So can you just lay out for me, what are these moving parts?
sentences.zh: 所以你能为我梳理一下吗，这些变数到底是什么？

sentences.en: What is the current state of play in Washington?
sentences.zh: 华盛顿目前的局势如何？

sentences.en: So I think the easiest way to think about this is for Democrats who control both the House and the Senate, this is a week where they are juggling two things.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得最简单的理解方式是，对于同时控制了众议院和参议院的民主党人来说，本周他们正在兼顾两件事。

sentences.en: They are juggling the basic fiscal responsibility of governance, the basic thing Congress always has to do every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们在兼顾治理的基本财政责任，也就是国会每年都必须做的基本事情。

sentences.en: And then they are juggling that with their own ambitious domestic proposal.
sentences.zh: 然后他们还要兼顾他们自己雄心勃勃的国内提案。

sentences.en: Well, let's start with the first thing, the basic governance stuff.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们先从第一件事开始，也就是基本的治理工作。

sentences.en: So the end of September is always a bit of a chaotic month for Congress because the fiscal year ends and they have to keep the government funded.
sentences.zh: 9月底对国会来说总是有点混乱的一个月，因为财政年度到期了，他们必须维持政府资金的运转。

sentences.en: On top of that, the Treasury Department has said that they are about to, in the next couple weeks, hit the limit on their ability to borrow.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，财政部表示，他们将在接下来的几周内触及借贷能力的上限。

sentences.en: And should Congress fail to address that in time, that could lead to a first-ever default on the federal debt, which could be fiscally catastrophic.
sentences.zh: 如果国会未能及时解决这个问题，可能会导致联邦债务有史以来第一次违约，这在财政上将是灾难性的。

sentences.en: And that is not an exaggeration.
sentences.zh: 这并不是夸大其词。

sentences.en: And as of Wednesday afternoon, Democrats and Republicans are currently talking about a short-term spending bill that would not only keep the government open through early December,
sentences.zh: 截至周三下午，民主党人和共和党人目前正在讨论一项短期支出法案，该法案不仅能让政府维持运转到12月初，

sentences.en: but provide pretty urgent emergency relief to help Afghan refugees and disaster recovery efforts across the country to pass that before funding runs out Thursday.
sentences.zh: 还将提供相当紧迫的紧急救援，以帮助阿富汗难民和全国各地的灾后恢复工作，并赶在资金在周四耗尽之前通过。

sentences.en: We expect Republicans to get on board with this short-term bill.
sentences.zh: 我们预计共和党人会加入支持这项短期法案的行列。

sentences.en: The debt ceiling, however, they have no interest in giving their votes, too.
sentences.zh: 然而，对于债务上限，他们毫无兴趣投赞成票。

sentences.en: So on the basic functionings of government, the thing that Congress must do, there is a likelihood that they'll keep the government open in the short term.
sentences.zh: 因此，在政府的基本职能方面，也就是国会必须要做的事情上，他们短期内保持政府运转的可能性很大。

sentences.en: And then the question of the debt ceiling,
sentences.zh: 然后关于债务上限的问题，

sentences.en: they're going to push that argument down the road with Democrats still trying to force Republicans to come to the table to do it with them together.
sentences.zh: 他们打算把这个争论往后推，而民主党人仍在试图迫使共和党人坐到谈判桌前与他们共同解决此事。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But you also said that the Biden agenda is in a pretty precarious situation.
sentences.zh: 但你也说过，拜登的议程处境相当岌岌可危。

sentences.en: What's exactly happening with that?
sentences.zh: 那到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: So, historically, the first year of a Congress is the best year to really try to push through any sort of ambitious policy.
sentences.zh: 从历史上看，国会的头一年是真正努力推动任何雄心勃勃的政策的最佳年份。

sentences.en: Because the closer you get to the next November election, the harder it is to bring people to the table while things are getting politically charged and competitive.
sentences.zh: 因为越接近接下来的11月选举，随着局势变得充满政治色彩和竞争激烈，把人们拉到谈判桌前就越困难。

sentences.en: So for President Biden, who oversees really narrow margins of a majority here, getting his agenda passed quickly is paramount.
sentences.zh: 因此，对于在这里仅拥有微弱多数席位优势的拜登总统来说，迅速通过他的议程至关重要。

sentences.en: Right now, there's two main pieces of this agenda.
sentences.zh: 目前，这个议程有两个主要部分。

sentences.en: There's this bipartisan infrastructure bill, which moderate Democrats helped negotiate, that would send billions of dollars for roads, bridges, broadband across the country.
sentences.zh: 一个是两党基础设施法案，温和派民主党人曾协助谈判该法案，它将向全国的道路、桥梁和宽带建设投入数十亿美元。

sentences.en: And then there's a second really ambitious package that contains a lot of the priorities that President Biden and Democrats ran on and believe helped deliver them the majority.
sentences.zh: 然后是第二个雄心勃勃得多的打包法案，其中包含许多拜登总统和民主党人在竞选时承诺、并认为正是这些帮助他们赢得多数席位的首要任务。

sentences.en: That proposed package right now is about $3.5 trillion.
sentences.zh: 目前提议的这个打包法案规模约为3.5万亿美元。

sentences.en: It would send money to address climate change.
sentences.zh: 它将拨款用于应对气候变化。

sentences.en: It would expand health care.
sentences.zh: 它将扩大医疗保健。

sentences.en: It would expand public education.
sentences.zh: 它将扩大公共教育。

sentences.en: It would touch almost every facet of American life.
sentences.zh: 它将触及美国生活的几乎方方面面。

sentences.en: And it would be paid for mostly with tax increases on wealthy businesses and wealthy individuals.
sentences.zh: 它将主要通过对富裕企业和富裕个人加税来支付资金。

sentences.en: In order to advance both of these pieces, congressional leaders agreed to this two-track process, in essence,
sentences.zh: 为了推进这两部分，国会领导层实质上同意了这种双轨进程，

sentences.en: accommodating progressives who said they would support the bipartisan bill, a bill that they felt was inadequate and not quite what they would have written,
sentences.zh: 以迎合那些表示愿意支持两党法案的进步派人士——这是一项他们认为不够完善、且不完全是他们自己会起草的法案——

sentences.en: in order to pass this much larger bill and get the entire party to come along with this much bigger agenda.
sentences.zh: 以此来通过这个规模大得多的法案，并让整个党派都接受这个更大的议程。

sentences.en: So as a way to keep the caucus together, to sort of maneuver around these very thin margins, party leaders effectively linked the two bills.
sentences.zh: 因此，为了保持党团的团结，为了在这些非常微弱的多数优势周围进行周旋，党内领导层实际上将这两项法案捆绑在了一起。

sentences.en: So we've been going along on this two-track process, that $1 trillion bipartisan infrastructure bill has passed the Senate.
sentences.zh: 所以我们一直沿着这个双轨进程前进，那项价值1万亿美元的两党基础设施法案已经在参议院获得通过。

sentences.en: It's waiting in the wings for a House vote.
sentences.zh: 它正蓄势待发等待众议院投票。

sentences.en: But when House Democrats tried to tackle just the process of beginning work on this $3.5 trillion package,
sentences.zh: 但当众议院民主党人试图着手处理启动这项3.5万亿美元法案的程序时，

sentences.en: a group of moderates said they would not support doing so until they got a commitment from Speaker Nancy Pelosi that she would hold a vote on the House infrastructure bill.
sentences.zh: 一小群温和派表示，在他们从众议院议长南希·佩洛西那里得到她将在众议院就基础设施法案举行投票的承诺之前，他们不会支持这样做。

sentences.en: And the date that they settled on was actually Monday, but then Speaker Pelosi pushed the date to Thursday, and then in a meeting with House Democrats seemed to suggest that she,
sentences.zh: 他们确定的日期其实是周一，但随后佩洛西议长将日期推迟到了周四，接着在与众议院民主党人的会议上似乎暗示她，

sentences.en: in essence, was going to decouple these two bills and move ahead with just the bipartisan infrastructure bill.
sentences.zh: 本质上，将把这两项法案脱钩，仅推进两党基础设施法案。

sentences.en: So in the original agreement, one side wanted the bipartisan infrastructure bill, and another side was more focused on the larger reconciliation bill.
sentences.zh: 所以在最初的协议中，一方想要两党基础设施法案，而另一方则更专注于更大的调和法案。

sentences.en: And so to appease both, the Speaker agreed to put them on a parallel track that they would try to be voted on at the same time.
sentences.zh: 为了安抚双方，议长同意将它们置于平行轨道上，试图同时对它们进行投票。

sentences.en: But the group of moderates who cared more about the infrastructure bill and are more skeptical of the reconciliation bill pushed the Speaker to change that agreement and actually disrupt that two-parallel track process?
sentences.zh: 但那一群更在乎基础设施法案、对调和法案更为怀疑的温和派，却敦促议长改变协议，实际上打乱了那个双平行轨道进程？

sentences.en: Pretty much.
sentences.zh: 差不多吧。

sentences.en: And as you can imagine, that was quite frustrating for the Progressive Caucus, which has close to 100 members.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象，这对拥有近100名成员的进步党团来说相当令人沮丧。

sentences.en: But progressives now, who have said for quite some time,
sentences.zh: 但进步派现在——他们一段时间以来一直表示，

sentences.en: we will not support that bill until we see progress on this bigger package with all of our desires and all of our ambitions, are really hesitating to vote for that.
sentences.zh: 在我们看到这个包含我们所有愿望和宏伟蓝图的更大打包法案取得进展之前，我们不会支持那项法案——现在真的很犹豫是否要投票支持它。

sentences.en: And they're repeatedly warning leadership, we can't vote for this until we see some progress.
sentences.zh: 他们一再警告领导层，在我们看到一些进展之前，我们不能投票支持这个。

sentences.en: Depending on the lawmaker you talk to and when you talk to them, that progress could be anything from a vote on a final package in the Senate,
sentences.zh: 取决于你跟哪位议员谈以及你是什么时候跟他们谈的，这种进展可以是各种各样的，从参议院对最终打包法案的投票——

sentences.en: which is a long ways off at this point because of so many outstanding policy issues,
sentences.zh: 由于有太多悬而未决的政策问题，目前离那一步还很远——

sentences.en: to just asking key moderates, particularly senators, Joe Manchin of West Virginia and Kyrsten Sinema of Arizona, to put forward a top line of what they would accept.
sentences.zh: 到仅仅要求关键温和派，特别是参议员西弗吉尼亚州的乔·曼钦和亚利桑那州的基尔斯滕·西内马，提出他们能够接受的总体上限。

sentences.en: Because that's been a big issue here.
sentences.zh: 因为这一直是这里的一个大问题。

sentences.en: Moderates, particularly these two senators, have signaled for a while now that $3.5 trillion is too high.
sentences.zh: 温和派，尤其是这两位参议员，一段时间以来一直暗示3.5万亿美元太高了。

sentences.en: They were okay starting a process for a package of that size, but ultimately they're not comfortable with that being the final product.
sentences.zh: 他们不反对为一个规模这么大的法案启动程序，但他们最终对这成为最终成果感到不舒服。

sentences.en: But what's less clear is what the moderates do want.
sentences.zh: 但不太清楚的是温和派究竟想要什么。

sentences.en: What price tag are they comfortable with?
sentences.zh: 他们能接受的价签是多少？

sentences.en: How do they want to scale back this vision that President Biden and liberals have laid out and have really championed for quite some time?
sentences.zh: 他们想如何缩减拜登总统和自由派勾勒出并大力倡导了相当长一段时间的这一宏伟愿景？

sentences.en: And it seems for some progressives, they've reached a point where it's just, just give us a sign that you want to support this package and just give us some sense of what you want,
sentences.zh: 在一些进步派看来，他们似乎已经到了这样一个地步：那就是，给我们一个信号，表明你们想支持这个打包法案，并让我们对你们想要什么有个大致概念，

sentences.en: what you're comfortable with at this point.
sentences.zh: 在这个时间点上你们能接受什么。

sentences.en: They just want a guarantee from their moderate colleagues that they will back a second package of the size and scope that they think is necessary to address the needs of the country and deliver on the promises they made to voters that they say got them this majority in the first place.
sentences.zh: 他们只想要来自温和派同僚的保证，即他们会支持一个规模和范围符合他们认为解决国家需求所需、并兑现他们对选民承诺的第二个打包法案，他们说正是这些承诺让他们最初赢得了这个多数席位。

sentences.en: If they hold firm, they could bring down this piece of legislation.
sentences.zh: 如果他们立场坚定，他们可能会让这项立法泡汤。

sentences.en: And I think this is an instance where people are looking to see, is this the moment where progressives really take a gamble here in holding firm?
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个人们拭目以待的时刻，看看这是否是进步派真正放手一搏、立场坚定的时刻？

sentences.en: After the break, I talked to Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal about that gamble.
sentences.zh: 休息过后，我与国会议员普拉米拉·贾亚帕尔谈了谈这场博弈。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到《重构者》，这是一个全方位探讨对设计的热爱以及与之相关的文化的播客。

sentences.zh: 甚至早在黑胶唱片时代的夜总会打碟时，你每天晚上都要带着300件你最珍爱的宝贝去上班。

sentences.en: And you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你把一个打碟台变成了一个美丽的50年历史文物的活体快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Hello, Congresswoman.
sentences.zh: 你好，议员女士。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: Good morning, Estet.
sentences.zh: 早上好，埃斯特。

sentences.en: I'm good.
sentences.zh: 我很好。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you for making this time out.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你腾出时间。

sentences.en: I know this is such a busy day.
sentences.zh: 我知道今天这么忙。

sentences.en: I'm curious.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇。

sentences.en: Is this your first meeting today or have you already started?
sentences.zh: 这是你今天的第一个会议，还是你已经开始忙了？

sentences.en: I have already started with phone calls and text messages, but it's my first meeting where I'm actually seeing somebody.
sentences.zh: 我已经在处理电话和短信了，但这确实是我今天第一次见到真人开会。

sentences.en: You know, we wanted to talk because all eyes are on you all and the House this week.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们想聊聊是因为本周所有人的目光都聚焦在你们和众议院身上。

sentences.en: There's that big bipartisan infrastructure bill that we know there will be a big vote on.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，将有一场针对那个大型两党基础设施法案的重要投票。

sentences.en: And as the head of the Progressive Caucus, you're the one in the room negotiating on the behalf of progressives.
sentences.zh: 作为进步党团的负责人，你是在房间里代表进步派进行谈判的人。

sentences.en: What does that look like?
sentences.zh: 那是个什么情况？

sentences.en: What are the stakes right now?
sentences.zh: 目前的利害关系是什么？

sentences.en: How does it feel in Congress?
sentences.zh: 在国会感觉如何？

sentences.en: Well, the stakes are very high, obviously, because we're talking about the president's agenda.
sentences.zh: 嗯，利害关系显然非常重大，因为我们讨论的是总统的议程。

sentences.en: We're talking about the Democratic agenda.
sentences.zh: 我们讨论的是民主党的议程。

sentences.en: We're talking about an agenda that we all ran on and are very invested in.
sentences.zh: 我们讨论的是一个我们所有人都在竞选时承诺过且投入极深的议程。

sentences.en: We are doing everything that we can to make sure we deliver the entirety of the agenda that already 96 percent of Democrats in the House and the Senate agree on.
sentences.zh: 我们正在竭尽全力确保交付议程的全部内容，众议院和参议院中已经有96%的民主党人对此表示赞同。

sentences.en: There's just a tiny contingent of people that are not with us yet.
sentences.zh: 只是有一小撮人还没有和我们站在一起。

sentences.en: And we are ready, willing and able to do everything possible to get to a final deal that gets us across the finish line.
sentences.zh: 我们已经准备好、愿意并且有能力尽一切可能达成最终协议，让我们冲过终点线。

sentences.en: And given those stakes, where would you describe Democrats are in this moment?
sentences.zh: 鉴于这些利害关系，你认为民主党人目前处于什么状态？

sentences.en: What is the current state of play at this point when it comes to the important piece of legislation?
sentences.zh: 当涉及到这份重要的立法时，目前的局势如何？

sentences.en: And we should note that we're talking to you at 9 a.m.
sentences.zh: 我们应该指出，我们是在周三上午9点与你交谈的，

sentences.en: on Wednesday, which I know these things will move quickly as the day goes on.
sentences.zh: 我知道随着时间的推移，这些事情会进展得很快。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And let me just back up and say, you know, that this moment that we're in, it's five months from April 28th, 2021,
sentences.zh: 让我回溯一下并指出，你知道，我们现在所处的这个时刻，距离2021年4月28日已经过去五个月了，

sentences.en: when the president came to Congress and delivered a speech on his agenda, on our agenda.
sentences.zh: 当时总统来到国会，发表了一场关于他的议程、关于我们的议程的演讲。

sentences.en: And that is what we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们正在谈论的。

sentences.en: That agenda got divided into two bills for anyone who hasn't followed this in detail.
sentences.zh: 对于任何没有详细关注此事的人来说，那个议程被拆分成了两个法案。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It got divided into a much smaller infrastructure bill that is about roads and highways.
sentences.zh: 它被拆分成了规模小得多、只关乎道路和高速公路的基础设施法案。

sentences.en: It's got some important stuff in it.
sentences.zh: 里面有一些重要的内容。

sentences.en: It's got some stuff that some of the progressives don't like because they feel it'll have a negative effect on climate.
sentences.zh: 里面有些内容是部分进步派不喜欢的，因为他们觉得会对气候产生负面影响。

sentences.en: And then the rest of the agenda was put into this Build Back Better Act.
sentences.zh: 然后议程的其余部分被放进了这个《重建更好法案》中。

sentences.en: And so what happened is that the Senate passed that bipartisan infrastructure bill with progressive senators there voting for it only because they were guaranteed that the reconciliation bill would go first in the House.
sentences.zh: 所以发生的事情是，参议院通过了那个两党基础设施法案，那里的进步派参议员之所以投票赞成，仅仅是因为他们得到了保证，即调和法案会在众议院率先通过。

sentences.en: And that's the Build Back Better Act with 70 percent of the president's agenda.
sentences.zh: 这就是包含总统70%议程的《重建更好法案》。

sentences.en: And so when it came to the House, all of a sudden there was a switcheroo.
sentences.zh: 所以当它来到众议院时，突然来了一个乾坤大挪移。

sentences.en: A small group of nine House Democrats said, no, all of a sudden we're going to put an arbitrary deadline of Monday, September 27th to have a vote first on the bipartisan bill.
sentences.zh: 一小群九名众议院民主党人表示，不，突然之间我们要设定一个9月27日星期一的专断死线，先对两党法案进行投票。

sentences.en: And then maybe we'll talk about the reconciliation bill.
sentences.zh: 然后我们再来谈调和法案。

sentences.en: A tiny group of people decided that they didn't like the agreement.
sentences.zh: 一小撮人决定他们不喜欢这个协议。

sentences.en: And so they went back on it and they said,
sentences.zh: 于是他们出尔反尔，并表示，

sentences.en: we're not going to vote for the budget resolution to even move forward on the discussion of the Build Back Better Act unless you vote for the bipartisan bill firSt.
sentences.zh: 除非你们先投票支持两党法案，否则我们不会投票支持预算决议案来推进对《重建更好法案》的讨论。

sentences.en: That didn't go over too well.
sentences.zh: 这可不太受欢迎。

sentences.en: We have said for three months that we're doing the reconciliation bill firSt.
sentences.zh: 我们三个月来一直说的是我们要先做调和法案。

sentences.en: That's what the Senate agreed to.
sentences.zh: 那是参议院同意的。

sentences.en: And so we have still continued to be in the same place,
sentences.zh: 所以我们依然保持在原有的立场上，

sentences.en: which is we understand that there has to be a negotiation on what is in the reconciliation bill with the small group of people that are saying they won't vote for it.
sentences.zh: 那就是我们理解必须与那一小群声称不会投票支持调和法案的人，就调和法案里的内容展开谈判。

sentences.en: We're open to doing that, but we need to hear what those people are for, not just what they're against, but what they're for.
sentences.zh: 我们对这样做持开放态度，但我们需要听听那些人是为了什么，不仅仅是他们反对什么，而是他们支持什么。

sentences.en: And until we get that firm commitment, vote in the Senate on the reconciliation bill, half of the progressive caucus, my members,
sentences.zh: 在我们得到坚定的承诺、参议院就调解法案进行投票之前，进步党团的一半成员，也就是我的同仁们，

sentences.en: have said they will not be able to vote for the infrastructure bill.
sentences.zh: 已经表示他们将无法投票赞成基础设施法案。

sentences.en: And so the fact that the progressive caucus said we will not vote for this bill made it so that that vote got canceled on Monday.
sentences.zh: 因此，进步党团表示我们不会投票支持这项法案，这导致周一的那场投票被取消了。

sentences.en: It's scheduled for tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 它定于明天举行。

sentences.en: We are all working hard to see if we can get to an agreement on a reconciliation bill.
sentences.zh: 我们都在努力工作，看看能否就调解法案达成一致。

sentences.en: But since we want a vote in the Senate, I think it's going to be very hard to get to that place by tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 但既然我们希望在参议院进行投票，我认为到明天很难走到这一步。

sentences.en: So when the speaker separated those bills, did you all read that as a betrayal or going back on your promises?
sentences.zh: 那么，当议长将这些法案分开时，你们是否认为这是一种背叛或出尔反尔？

sentences.en: I know there were some members of the progressive caucus who did describe those actions of Pelosi like that.
sentences.zh: 我知道进步党团确实有一些成员这样形容佩洛西的那些举动。

sentences.en: I know there are some members who described it that way.
sentences.zh: 我知道有一些成员是这样形容的。

sentences.en: I don't yet see it that way because I have been talking to the speaker and I think she wants the same things that we do.
sentences.zh: 我目前还没有这样看，因为我一直在与议长沟通，而且我认为她想要的东西和我们一样。

sentences.en: And I think that she is, you know, working to try to get everybody moving as quickly as possible in the same direction.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为她，你知道的，正在努力让每个人都以最快的速度朝着同一个方向前进。

sentences.en: But I don't think that she's going to bring a bill to the floor.
sentences.zh: 但我不认为她会将法案提交表决。

sentences.en: And if she does, I'll just tell you, if she does,
sentences.zh: 如果她真的这么做了，我直接告诉你，如果她真的这么做了，

sentences.en: we have more than enough members to defeat the bill and show whoever's wondering whether she has the votes that it's not going to pass until we do the reconciliation bill.
sentences.zh: 我们有足够多的成员来否决该法案，并向任何怀疑她是否拥有票数的人表明，在我们完成调解法案之前，它是不会通过的。

sentences.en: But do you agree that the decision to split those up does place a kind of pressure on progressives?
sentences.zh: 但你是否同意，拆分它们的决定确实给进步派施加了一种压力？

sentences.en: It is now up to you all if that bill comes up on Thursday to make the decision about whether to doom the bipartisan infrastructure bill when it votes the House.
sentences.zh: 如果该法案在周四提交表决，现在就由你们来决定是否在众议院投票时扼杀两党基础设施法案。

sentences.en: How does it feel that that is now in you all's laps?
sentences.zh: 现在这一切落到了你们头上，你们有什么感觉？

sentences.en: Does it make you upset that it is now your choice instead of the Joe Manchin's and Kyrsten Sinema's in the Senate?
sentences.zh: 这难道不让你们感到沮丧吗？现在是你们而不是参议院的乔·曼钦和基尔斯滕·西内马来做选择。

sentences.en: Not really.
sentences.zh: 其实还好。

sentences.en: I actually think we've been the ones who have been saving the president's agenda for months.
sentences.zh: 我实际上认为，几个月来一直拯救总统议程的是我们。

sentences.en: We are the ones who have been standing up to deliver on the president's agenda for months.
sentences.zh: 几个月来，挺身而出落实总统议程的是我们。

sentences.en: And I think we will accept the responsibility of delivering to voters what we promised them, the democratic agenda.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为我们将承担起责任，将我们向选民承诺的民主党议程交付给他们。

sentences.en: And so we're proud to deliver both bills.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们很自豪能够通过这两项法案。

sentences.en: There are many, as I said, many members of our caucus who don't want to vote for the infrastructure bill because they think it's a bad bill.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，我们党团中有许多成员不想投票支持基础设施法案，因为他们认为这是一项糟糕的法案。

sentences.en: But every single one of them has been an adult in the room and said, we are willing to vote for something we don't like, that we actually think may not be good for our goals.
sentences.zh: 但他们中的每一个人都表现得像个成熟的大人，并表示，我们愿意投票支持我们不喜欢的东西，甚至是我们认为可能对我们的目标不利的东西。

sentences.en: But we understand we're part of the democratic team.
sentences.zh: 但我们明白我们是民主党团队的一员。

sentences.en: And that's 96 percent of the democratic caucus, by the way, is with us.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，进步党团百分之九十六的人都和我们站在一起。

sentences.en: This is not a progressives versus moderates fight.
sentences.zh: 这不是进步派与温和派的斗争。

sentences.en: This is a president's agenda versus 4 percent of Democrats fight.
sentences.zh: 这是总统议程与百分之四的民主党人的斗争。

sentences.en: I get that.
sentences.zh: 我懂的。

sentences.en: And I get that with all of these moving targets, how you all have an interest in saying if the bipartisan bill comes to the floor,
sentences.zh: 我明白，面对所有这些不断变化的目标，你们为什么会有兴趣表示，如果两党法案提交表决，

sentences.en: we're not going to vote for it in hopes of getting that agenda passed.
sentences.zh: 为了通过那个议程，我们不会投票支持它。

sentences.en: But we know that most folks in the country do not follow these things as closely as we do.
sentences.zh: 但我们知道，国内大多数人并不像我们这样密切关注这些事情。

sentences.en: Are you worried at all that there is a risk of a headline that says, hey, progressives have doomed this negotiated bipartisan bill that would improve infrastructure in America?
sentences.zh: 你们是否担心会出现这样一种头条新闻的风险，即嘿，进步派扼杀了好不容易谈妥的、旨在改善美国基础设施的两党法案？

sentences.en: I would say two things to that.
sentences.zh: 对此我想说两点。

sentences.en: One, the bipartisan bill can always be brought up again.
sentences.zh: 第一，两党法案随时可以重新提交。

sentences.en: You know, the Senate has passed it already.
sentences.zh: 你知道，参议院已经通过了它。

sentences.en: If it goes down now, we give this negotiation a little bit more time and we get to a deal on reconciliation.
sentences.zh: 如果它现在倒下了，我们给这场谈判更多一点时间，并就调解达成协议。

sentences.en: We can always bring up the bipartisan bill again.
sentences.zh: 我们随时可以再次提出两党法案。

sentences.en: So whatever happens tomorrow or doesn't happen tomorrow isn't the end of the story.
sentences.zh: 所以明天发生什么或不发生什么并不是故事的结局。

sentences.en: And it shouldn't be.
sentences.zh: 也不应该是。

sentences.en: These are arbitrary dates.
sentences.zh: 这些都是随意的日期。

sentences.en: But the second thing is I think we have to just understand that if we leave behind what is in the reconciliation bill, the Build Back Better Act, it delays that.
sentences.zh: 但第二点是，我认为我们必须明白，如果我们把调解法案（即《重建更好法案》）中的内容抛在脑后，这就会推迟它。

sentences.en: We are now in September.
sentences.zh: 我们现在已经到了九月。

sentences.en: And for anyone who watches Congress, it's hard enough to get things done when you have momentum, when you don't have momentum,
sentences.zh: 对于任何关注国会的人来说，当你拥有势头时把事情做好已经够难了，而当你没有势头时，

sentences.en: when it's the end of the year before an election year, or if it goes over into December, January, February of next year, nothing gets done around here.
sentences.zh: 当它处于选举年之前的一年年底时，或者如果它拖到明年的十二月、一月、二月，这里什么事情也办不成。

sentences.en: So I want everybody to understand that if we vote for the bipartisan bill, hoping and praying that perhaps there will be some agreement on reconciliation,
sentences.zh: 所以我希望每个人都明白，如果我们投票支持两党法案，同时又心存侥幸和祈祷，希望就调解达成某种协议，

sentences.en: that is not a hope that is borne out by any evidence.
sentences.zh: 这种希望没有任何证据来支撑。

sentences.en: We have sent over dozens of bills to the Senate, including voting rights bills that really need to be passed right now if we want to save our democracy.
sentences.zh: 我们已经向参议院发送了数十项法案，包括如果我们想拯救民主就必须立即通过的投票权法案。

sentences.en: And yet those have not been passed.
sentences.zh: 然而这些法案尚未通过。

sentences.en: So delay means death.
sentences.zh: 所以延迟就等于死亡。

sentences.en: And that is why we can't let go of these two things moving together in tandem.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们不能放手让这两件事并行推进。

sentences.en: But how do you square a delay means death on the reconciliation bill while also saying you're willing to delay the bipartisan infrastructure bill?
sentences.zh: 但是，一方面说调解法案延迟就等于死亡，另一方面又说你愿意延迟两党基础设施法案，你该如何调和这一点？

sentences.en: Do you see those things as in conflict?
sentences.zh: 你认为这些事情是冲突的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a great question.
sentences.zh: 对，这是一个好问题。

sentences.en: No, because the infrastructure bill has already been negotiated.
sentences.zh: 不，因为基础设施法案已经谈判好了。

sentences.en: Not with us, I might add.
sentences.zh: 请允许我补充一句，不是和我们谈判的。

sentences.en: It was negotiated by a very small group of people who then expected us to just take that.
sentences.zh: 它是由一小群人谈判达成的，然后他们希望我们全盘接受。

sentences.en: When we tried to do the same thing with the reconciliation bill and say this is the president's agenda, 96 percent agree, you should come along, they said, no,
sentences.zh: 当我们试图对调解法案做同样的事情并说这是总统的议程，百分之九十六的人赞同，你们应该加入时，他们说，不，

sentences.en: we're not going to do that.
sentences.zh: 我们不打算这么做。

sentences.en: So there's no problem with bringing the bipartisan bill up immediately if we get a deal on the reconciliation bill because it already passed the Senate.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们就能调解法案达成协议，立即提出两党法案是没有问题的，因为它已经通过了参议院。

sentences.en: We've already agreed and committed to doing it.
sentences.zh: 我们已经同意并承诺这样做了。

sentences.en: We actually gave in and compromised on that.
sentences.zh: 我们在这一点上确实作出了让步和妥协。

sentences.en: And now it's time for the 4 percent to do a real negotiation with the 96 percent and say, OK, we want to do these things and then we're ready to go forward.
sentences.zh: 现在是那百分之四的人与百分之九十六的人进行真正谈判的时候了，他们应该说，好吧，我们想做这些事情，然后我们就准备前行了。

sentences.en: And I'll just say if we don't deliver on this agenda, we won't have control of the Senate.
sentences.zh: 我只想说，如果我们未能兑现这个议程，我们就将失去对参议院的控制。

sentences.en: We won't have control of the House and we won't have the White House back.
sentences.zh: 我们将失去对众议院的控制，我们也拿不回白宫。

sentences.en: So you're saying that the politics of this are clear to you that the most vulnerable people in the midterms need that full agenda to be passed and that the bipartisan bill would not be good enough for really to them go back to their voters and say,
sentences.zh: 所以你是说，这里的政治形势对你们来说很明朗，中期选举中最脆弱的人需要完整的议程得以通过，而两党法案对他们来说还不够好，无法真正向选民承诺说，

sentences.en: this is what we did with the Democratic House, Senate and White House.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们在拥有民主党控制的众议院、参议院和白宫时所做的事情。

sentences.en: But what if progressives get neither of those rather than both of those done?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果进步派两边都没办成，而不是两边都办成了呢？

sentences.en: Is that a risk that you all are willing to take that in pursuit of getting both of the things done, that there could be a situation where both of them are delayed?
sentences.zh: 为了两件事都能办成，可能会出现两件事都被推迟的情况，你们愿意承担这种风险吗？

sentences.en: It's always a risk.
sentences.zh: 这总是伴随着风险。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, negotiation does not come without risk and standing up for things that people really need.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道的，谈判不可能没有风险，为人们真正需要的事物挺身而出也是如此。

sentences.en: It's time for us to stand up and deliver deeply needed investments that will transform the way that people see their lives and their livelihoods.
sentences.zh: 现在是我们挺身而出的时候了，要落实急需的投资，这些投资将改变人们看待生活和生计的方式。

sentences.en: So you're willing to take that argument to the American people that you all made this decision,
sentences.zh: 所以你们愿意把这个论点带给美国人民，即你们做出了这个决定，

sentences.en: even if it results in the bipartisan infrastructure bill not passing this week because you think fighting for the full agenda is where the public is?
sentences.zh: 即使它导致两党基础设施法案本周未能通过，因为你们认为为完整议程而战才是民意所在？

sentences.en: I think that's absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 我认为这绝对是正确的。

sentences.en: There is a president now, though, that campaigned on reaching across the aisle, that campaigned on kind of bringing unity and bipartisanship back to Washington.
sentences.zh: 不过，现在有一位总统，他的竞选纲领是跨越党派分歧，致力于将团结和两党合作带回华盛顿。

sentences.en: Is a vote against the bipartisan infrastructure bill a blow to the Democratic president's own rhetoric and words?
sentences.zh: 投反对两党基础设施法案的票，是对这位民主党总统自己的言辞和承诺的打击吗？

sentences.en: The entire agenda not passing is a serious blow to our president.
sentences.zh: 整个议程未能通过对我们的总统来说是一个沉重的打击。

sentences.en: And he said that very clearly when he brought us into the Oval Office.
sentences.zh: 当他把我们请进椭圆形办公室时，他非常明确地表达了这一点。

sentences.en: He said it to me directly.
sentences.zh: 他直接对我说过。

sentences.en: I think that the reality is he wants both bills to pass.
sentences.zh: 我认为现实情况是他希望这两项法案都能通过。

sentences.en: And he's been very clear about that over and over again.
sentences.zh: 他一次又一次地非常明确地表达了这一点。

sentences.en: Is there any frustration from progressives then?
sentences.zh: 那么进步派有什么挫败感吗？

sentences.en: Do you want the White House to be coming out more or engaging more publicly in pressuring Senator Manchin and Sinema?
sentences.zh: 你们希望白宫更多地站出来，或者更多地公开参与，向曼钦和西内马参议员施压吗？

sentences.en: Well, I think they are doing that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为他们正在这样做。

sentences.en: Not all work happens in the public eye.
sentences.zh: 并非所有的工作都发生在公众视野中。

sentences.en: In fact, it's not always advisable.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这并不总是明智的。

sentences.en: You know, the White House and the president have a very different role.
sentences.zh: 你知道，白宫和总统扮演着非常不同的角色。

sentences.en: They got to bring everyone together.
sentences.zh: 他们必须把每个人凝聚在一起。

sentences.en: You're right that that is what he ran on is his ability to reach across the aisle.
sentences.zh: 你说得对，他的竞选卖点就是他跨越党派分歧的能力。

sentences.en: I think that's important, the work that they're doing.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是重要的，他们正在做的工作。

sentences.en: And I do think they're very actively engaged.
sentences.zh: 而且我确实认为他们非常积极地参与其中。

sentences.en: I will say that I told them, I don't know,
sentences.zh: 我要说的是，我曾经告诉过他们，不知道是，

sentences.en: three and a half months ago that they needed to engage on the reconciliation bill and the Build Back Better Act and getting people to a place that they agreed.
sentences.zh: 三个半月前，他们就需要参与到调解法案和《重建更好法案》中来，让大家达成共识。

sentences.en: And they were fully focused on the bipartisan bill, which, you know, I understand that was a choice they made.
sentences.zh: 而他们当时全神贯注于两党法案，你知道的，我理解那是他们做出的选择。

sentences.en: But you can't expect to just be able to get this thing done when we have a couple of people blocking.
sentences.zh: 但当我们有几个人在从中作梗时，你不能指望轻而易举地把这事办成。

sentences.en: It is going to take some time.
sentences.zh: 这需要一些时间。

sentences.en: And putting arbitrary deadlines in just hurts the process.
sentences.zh: 设定随意的最后期限只会损害这一进程。

sentences.en: And going back on agreements that were made doesn't help either because at the end of the day, we got to start trusting each other.
sentences.zh: 违背已经达成的协议也无济于事，因为到头来，我们必须开始相互信任。

sentences.en: And right now, you know, I would say we're in the verify mode.
sentences.zh: 而现在，你知道的，我想说我们正处于核实模式。

sentences.en: It's not the trust mode anymore.
sentences.zh: 不再是信任模式了。

sentences.en: It's just the verify mode.
sentences.zh: 现在只是核实模式。

sentences.en: And I understand that.
sentences.zh: 我理解这一点。

sentences.en: And I understand that you are being very diplomatic about it.
sentences.zh: 我也理解你对此表现得非常外交辞令。

sentences.en: But I want to ask again, you mentioned how three and a half months ago you were saying that the White House needed to focus more on the reconciliation front, on the agenda front,
sentences.zh: 但我想再问一次，你提到三个半月前你曾说过白宫需要把更多精力放在调解阵线、议程阵线上，

sentences.en: than the bipartisan bill.
sentences.zh: 而不是两党法案上。

sentences.en: And they didn't do it.
sentences.zh: 而他们没有这样做。

sentences.en: You're saying that the White House has been applying private pressure on the senators.
sentences.zh: 你说白宫一直在对参议员施加私下压力。

sentences.en: But publicly, a lot of the pressure is falling on progressives now with this Thursday vote.
sentences.zh: 但在公众面前，随着周四的这次投票，很多压力现在都落在了进步派身上。

sentences.en: I am wondering how those things don't add up to a White House that has put you all in a position to be a public face of maybe a tough, tough vote that some folks,
sentences.zh: 我想知道为什么这些情况没有指向一个事实：白宫把你们置于这样一个位置，让你们去当公众形象，去面对一场可能非常艰难的投票，而有些人——

sentences.en: even in your own party, may not love.
sentences.zh: 甚至在你们自己的党内——可能并不喜欢这样。

sentences.en: Well, look, every one of these positions is tough.
sentences.zh: 嗯，听着，每一个这样的立场都很艰难。

sentences.en: But I just think that you have to be driven by what you came here to do.
sentences.zh: 但我只是认为，你必须由你来这里的初心所驱动。

sentences.en: Is some of this not about policy, but politics?
sentences.zh: 其中有些不涉及政策，而是关乎政治吗？

sentences.en: Is some of this a progressive caucus saying, you know, you can't take us for granted anymore?
sentences.zh: 其中有些是进步党团在说，你知道的，你们不能再把我们视为理所当然了吗？

sentences.en: Well, I don't think that that position is ever just about politics, like, separated from policy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不认为这种立场仅仅关乎政治而脱离了政策。

sentences.en: I think it's always tied to policy.
sentences.zh: 我认为它总是与政策息息相关。

sentences.en: See, I'm not one to pick every single battle.
sentences.zh: 你看，我不是那种每场仗都要打的人。

sentences.en: I'm one to pick our fights carefully because I think it is challenging to explain what's going on to the American people.
sentences.zh: 我是那种会谨慎选择战斗的人，因为我认为向美国人民解释到底发生了什么具有挑战性。

sentences.en: And you do have to win the narrative.
sentences.zh: 而且你必须赢得叙事的主导权。

sentences.en: And I feel like we're winning the narrative right now.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们现在正赢得叙事的主导权。

sentences.en: What gives you that confidence?
sentences.zh: 是什么让你有这种信心？

sentences.en: I'm curious.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇。

sentences.en: Because I think if you look at the polling on the Build Back Better agenda, it's so darn good.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为如果你看看关于“重建更好”议程的民调，它好得不得了。

sentences.en: And actually, it's not only that 70 percent of Americans support it, but on top of that,
sentences.zh: 事实上，不仅百分之七十的美国人支持它，最重要的是，

sentences.en: if you add that you're going to tax the wealthiest individuals and the wealthiest corporations to pay their fair share, that number goes even higher.
sentences.zh: 如果你加上要对最富有的人和最富有的企业征税以让他们支付公平份额这一条，这个支持率还会更高。

sentences.en: You mentioned how you find the deadlines arbitrary, but this window will close eventually.
sentences.zh: 你提到你觉得最后期限是随意的，但这个窗口最终会关闭。

sentences.en: When do you think that is?
sentences.zh: 你认为那会是什么时候？

sentences.en: By what point do Democrats need to be able to say this agenda has been passed, the infrastructure bill has been passed, and turn to the other things,
sentences.zh: 民主党人需要在什么时间点之前能够宣布，这个议程已经通过了，基础设施法案已经通过了，然后转向其他那些——

sentences.en: which we're not even talking about, that haven't been resolved, like voting rights, like other parts, that were key portions of what Biden pitched to the American people?
sentences.zh: 我们甚至都还没谈到、且尚未解决的事情，比如投票权，比如作为拜登向美国人民推销的关键部分的其它部分？

sentences.en: Well, I don't know what the answer is to that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不知道这个问题的答案是什么。

sentences.en: I don't think we have a lot of time.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们没有多少时间了。

sentences.en: I think maybe we have a month or two to finish this all off.
sentences.zh: 我想我们可能只有一两个月来完成这一切。

sentences.en: Hopefully, it's just a couple of weeks.
sentences.zh: 希望只需要几个星期。

sentences.en: But your point about voting rights is really important.
sentences.zh: 但你关于投票权的观点真的很重要。

sentences.en: If we allow a couple of people to derail the Democratic agenda on the Build Back Better Act, what does it say about our ability to get voting rights?
sentences.zh: 如果我们允许几个人破坏民主党关于《重建更好法案》的议程，这说明我们争取投票权的能力如何？

sentences.en: What does it say about our ability to get police reform?
sentences.zh: 这说明我们争取警察改革的能力如何？

sentences.en: What does it say about our ability to get anything that we want?
sentences.zh: 这说明我们争取任何我们想要的东西的能力如何？

sentences.en: Because we know that that is the block in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 因为我们知道那是参议院的阻碍所在。

sentences.en: In my time as an activist, I spent 20 years as an organizer on the outside.
sentences.zh: 在我担任活动家的那段时期，我在体制外做了20年的组织工作。

sentences.en: I had something I would always tell young organizers that came in.
sentences.zh: 我过去常常对新加入的年轻组织者说一句话。

sentences.en: Two things, actually.
sentences.zh: 实际上是两句话。

sentences.en: One is that if politics is the art of the possible, because people always used to say that to me, Pramila, you have to be realistic.
sentences.zh: 一句是，如果政治是可能的艺术——因为人们总是对我说这话，普米拉，你必须现实一点，

sentences.en: Politics is the art of the possible.
sentences.zh: 政治是可能的艺术。

sentences.en: And I would say to organizers, if politics is the art of the possible, then it's our job as organizers and activists, wherever we sit, whether it's inside government or outside,
sentences.zh: 我会对组织者说，如果政治是可能的艺术，那么无论我们身在何处，是在政府内部还是在体制外，作为组织者和活动家，我们的工作就是

sentences.en: to push the boundaries of what is seen as possible.
sentences.zh: 突破被视为可能的界限。

sentences.en: Because the possible is not static.
sentences.zh: 因为所谓的“可能”并不是一成不变的。

sentences.en: It moves all the time.
sentences.zh: 它时刻都在变化。

sentences.en: And the second is that courage is born out of crisis.
sentences.zh: 其次是，勇气诞生于危机之中。

sentences.en: And it is a muscle.
sentences.zh: 而且它就像是一块肌肉。

sentences.en: You have to learn to flex it.
sentences.zh: 你必须学会去锻炼它。

sentences.en: When people see courage, the more it's exhibited, the more other people demonstrate it.
sentences.zh: 当人们看到勇气时，它展现得越多，其他人就越能表现出勇气。

sentences.en: And I think it's important for us to stand up for working people and for poor people across this country who desperately need us to do that.
sentences.zh: 我认为，我们必须挺身而出，为这个国家的劳动人民和穷人发声，他们迫切需要我们这么做。

sentences.en: If the end of this is a stripped-down reconciliation bill that you all are forced to compromise even further from $6 trillion down, has that been a failure of that vision?
sentences.zh: 如果这一切最终演变成一项被大幅削减的和解法案，迫使你们在6万亿美元的基础上做出进一步妥协，那么这是否意味着这种愿景的失败？

sentences.en: How has that been a failure to expand what is possible even among a unified Democrat Congress and White House?
sentences.zh: 在即使拥有统一的民主党国会和白宫的情况下，未能扩大可能性，这怎么能不算是一种失败呢？

sentences.en: Well, we're only going to agree to something that we think is not a failure, something that really allows us to claim success.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们只会同意那些我们认为不算失败、真正能让我们宣称取得成功的事情。

sentences.en: But I would just say the entire conversation has changed.
sentences.zh: 但我只想说，整个对话的语境已经变了。

sentences.en: I mean, the fact that we're even talking about these things as the Democratic agenda was not the case 10 years ago, as you know.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，正如你所知，10年前我们根本不会把这些事情当作民主党议程来讨论。

sentences.en: And so I feel like this moment is a success because the party has adopted core progressive platforms and ideas, including that the rich need to pay their fair share.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得现在这个时刻就是一种成功，因为党已经采纳了核心的进步派纲领和理念，包括富人需要缴纳他们应尽的份额。

sentences.en: And it's coming straight from the president's mouth.
sentences.zh: 而且这是直接从总统口中说出来的。

sentences.en: It's not coming from just the leader of the Progressive Caucus or our most progressive members.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅来自进步党团领袖或我们最激进的成员。

sentences.en: It's coming from the president of the United States who was elected in a phenomenally stunning victory and a mandate from black women and poor people and immigrants in states that he never thought he could win.
sentences.zh: 这是来自美国总统，他在黑人女性、穷人以及他在从未想过能获胜的州中的移民的支持下，以惊人的压倒性胜利和民意授权当选。

sentences.en: We delivered that victory.
sentences.zh: 我们赢得了这场胜利。

sentences.en: We delivered that mandate.
sentences.zh: 我们传达了这份民意。

sentences.en: And I believe he is absolutely with us, 100 percent with us on this set of issues.
sentences.zh: 我相信他在这一系列问题上绝对与我们站在一起，百分之百与我们站在一起。

sentences.en: It is a great kind of twist of what you're saying, that you're describing the success as getting the Democratic Party and the president to kind of agree on these baseline issues.
sentences.zh: 这其实是你刚才说的一种大反转，你把成功描述为让民主党和总统在这些底线问题上达成一致。

sentences.en: But the fact that it's 96 percent and not 100 percent is currently stopping you all from making that happen and making that a reality.
sentences.zh: 但正是因为达到了96%而不是100%，目前才阻碍了你们将这一切付诸实施、变成现实。

sentences.en: Yes, that is that is exactly right.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全是这样。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The four percent are stopping the 96 percent.
sentences.zh: 4%的人阻碍了96%的人。

sentences.en: And that's why we are holding strong, because we've got the majority with us, not just of Congress, but of the American people.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们要立场坚定，因为我们不仅拥有国会多数派的支持，还拥有美国人民的支持。

sentences.en: So what do you think happens on Thursday?
sentences.zh: 那你觉得周四会发生什么？

sentences.en: Do you think the bill comes to a vote?
sentences.zh: 你认为法案会提交表决吗？

sentences.en: And if so, what's your caucus going to do?
sentences.zh: 如果是的话，你们的党团打算怎么做？

sentences.en: If I had to bet, I would say the bill doesn't come to a vote.
sentences.zh: 如果非要我打赌，我会说该法案不会提交表决。

sentences.en: And we continue negotiating on the reconciliation bill.
sentences.zh: 我们将继续就和解法案进行谈判。

sentences.en: If it does come to a vote, it will go down and we will go back to the drawing board.
sentences.zh: 如果它真的提交表决了，它就会被否决，然后我们将重新回到画板前。

sentences.en: So you're saying that either way,
sentences.zh: 所以你的意思是，无论如何，

sentences.en: you are confident that the progressive caucus will hold and that either the bill will be delayed because of that or it will fail on the floor because you all will stick together.
sentences.zh: 你都坚信进步派党团会团结一致，要么法案因此被延期，要么因为你们团结一心而在众议院遭遇失败。

sentences.en: That's correct.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Well, thank you, Congressman.
sentences.zh: 好的，谢谢你，众议员。

sentences.en: We really appreciate your time and we know it's a busy day.
sentences.zh: 我们非常感谢你抽出时间，我们也知道今天你很忙。

sentences.en: So thank you.
sentences.zh: 所以谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: On Wednesday, United Airlines announced that it would fire nearly 600 workers for refusing to comply with its vaccine mandate,
sentences.zh: 周三，联合航空宣布将解雇近600名拒绝遵守疫苗接种强制令的员工，

sentences.zh: 该航空公司表示，这600人仅占其在美国6.7万名员工中的一小部分，并称其99%的美国

sentences.en: employees had been vaccinated.
sentences.zh: 员工已经接种了疫苗。
